text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub said Pakistan will match India's missile programme adding that a unilateral cut in defence spending would be suicidal.
- Pakistani and Indian border guards exchanged fire late Tuesday night, leaving a major of Pakistan rengers killed and unknown casualties on the Indian side, military officials said.
- The government has formed a committee to determine whether a foreign ship dumped toxic material into the sea near Gadani in Balochistan province.
THE MUSLIM
- One person was shot dead and three were critically wounded when a gunman terrorist opened fire at a mosque in Lahore.
THE FRONTIER POST
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub will visit Central Asian Republics from June 18 to 20 to promote regional understanding on the Afghan crisis.
THE NATION
- A Pakistani air force fighter aircraft crashed during a routine training flight at Athara Hazari in district Jhang in northern Punjab.
- The British Council has commissioned a senior British police officer to investigate leakage of question papers of "A-level" examinations.
- Railway employees observed a black day to protest against the government's privatisation plans and a proposed ban on labour unions.
DAWN

- Financial 1996/97 (July-June) was one of the worst years in Pakistan's history when all major economic indicators dropped alarmingly. GDP (gross domestic product) grew 3.1 percent, agriculture 0.7 percent and manufacturing 1.8 percent, the Economic Survey for 1996/97 said.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif pledged to do away with the existing system of exploitation by bringing about radical changes to ensure social justice and prosperity.
- The rate of inflation for 12 months ending May has been estimated at 11.63 percent.
- The trade gap for the 11 months to May shot up to $3.15 billion compared to $2.97 billion in the same period a year ago.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Customs have stopped accepting Bills of Entry a week ahead of Friday's 1997/98 budget.
FINANCIAL POST
- The stage is set for the privatisation of Habib Credit and Exchange Bank Ltd on Thursday.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
